iterations.prompt:
# Art Style

Render as a clean, modern, FLAT comic illustration in the style of the "At His Command"
reference art: bold, sharp, high-contrast, and completely smooth. This is a crisp DIGITAL
vector-style illustration — NOT a photograph, and NOT a textured, printed, or vintage page.

## Rendering — this is the most important part
- **Flat color fills:** Every shape is filled with ONE perfectly smooth, uniform, solid flat
  color, like a flat vector fill. Large fields — the background, walls, clothing, desk, screens
  — are each a single solid color, edge to edge. There is ABSOLUTELY NO surface texture
  anywhere in the image: no grain, no noise, no speckle, no dithering, no paper / canvas /
  newsprint / parchment / aged look, and no print or ink texture — including on the borders,
  the background, and every panel. Surfaces are as clean and smooth as flat digital color.
- **Linework:** Bold, confident, SHARP, clean black ink outlines with varied weight — heavy
  contour lines around the forms, crisp interior lines. Detail is carried by LINE only, never
  by texture or by rendered shading.
- **Shading:** Simple hard-edged cel shading — at most TWO flat tones per surface (a base flat
  color plus ONE darker flat tone), with clean hard shadow edges and solid black shadow shapes.
  NO gradients, NO blends, NO airbrush, NO halftone or Ben-Day dots, NO cross-hatching.
- **Borders & background:** Panel borders and the background are solid flat color fields with
  clean edges — flat and smooth, never textured.

## Text & Furniture
- Render ONLY the text specified for the composition — exact wording, nothing else.
- Caption boxes and banners are flat solid fills with clean black borders and bold, confident
  hand-lettered type. The title is bold block lettering on a jagged burst, like the "At His
  Command" masthead.

## Mood
Bold, clean, sharp, high-impact, optimistic — it reads instantly from across the room, exactly
like the "At His Command" art.

# Color Palette

A warm-dominant, high-energy **orange-and-blue complementary palette** extracted from the
"At His Command" comic cover: a glowing golden-amber field carries the image, burnt-orange
shadows model the warm forms, and cool steel-blue and deep navy provide the complementary
accent — borders, machine chassis, and the deepest shadows. Black ink anchors everything and
cream carries any text furniture.

**Balance:** roughly **70% warm / 30% cool** — orange and gold dominate the large areas; blue
is the accent that frames, cools the shadows, and makes the warms pop by contrast. Red is a
spark, used only for a few high-impact hits (title, a signal light). Do not let blue take over
large fields — it belongs on edges, machinery, and shadow.

## Swatches

Warm (dominant):
- **Golden Amber** `#F9C233` — the primary background field / lit warm surfaces; bright, sunny.
- **Marigold** `#F9B41E` — secondary warm, warm midtones and glow.
- **Burnt Orange** `#C96A10` — warm shadow and modeled form on the gold; the main orange.
- **Sienna** `#9A4E12` — deep warm shadow, wood, grounded warmth.
- **Signal Red** `#CC1616` — accent only: display type, a warning light, a spark. Use sparingly.

Cool (complementary accent):
- **Steel Blue** `#175E8C` — cool accent: panel borders, robot/machine chassis, cool props.
- **Deep Navy** `#16223C` — the coolest, deepest shadows, panel gutters, a bottom bar.

Neutrals / anchors:
- **Ink Black** `#101010` — linework, heavy contour, panel borders. Anchors the whole image.
- **Cream** `#FBE5A0` — caption boxes, paper highlights, text-furniture fill.
- **Warm Wood Brown** `#6E451F` — supporting neutral for wood/surfaces; keeps neutrals warm.

## How to apply
- Build large areas out of the golden amber → burnt orange → sienna warm ramp; reserve steel
  blue and deep navy for edges, machinery, and shadow so the complementary contrast stays sharp.
- Keep shadows **warm-to-cool**: warm forms fall into burnt orange, then into deep navy at the
  darkest core — never into muddy gray.
- Let blue and orange sit directly against each other at focal points for maximum pop.
- Red is a garnish, not a field — a couple of deliberate hits at most.
- Keep neutrals warm (cream, wood brown, ink black); avoid cool grays, which flatten the scheme.

# Composition

One kid, one robot, one big emotion — a poster-style hero shot built around a single beat.

## Layout
- A central figure in a bold, confident pose, with the robot as the second focal point.
- Clean, uncluttered composition — nothing extraneous; purposeful negative space.
- A burst / starburst speech balloon carrying one short, punchy line.
- A thin caption strip along the bottom is available for a marketing line.

## Feel
Iconic and immediate — the viewer's eye hits the face first, then the robot. Designed to
work as a standalone social/web image or the front of a card.

# Scene

WIDE LANDSCAPE 4x6 postcard (3:2). Over-the-shoulder view FROM BEHIND of TWO mid-teen students (about 14-15), large in the foreground and pushed to the extreme EDGES: a teenage boy at the FAR LEFT and a teenage girl at the FAR RIGHT, partly cropped off-page, bookending the shot. TWO large monitors dominate the CENTER on a wide desk spanning the full width. The boy leans in and points a pen at the LEFT monitor; the girl's hands are on the keyboard. LEFT MONITOR: a San Diego HEAT MAP — a recognizable San Diego shape (Pacific coastline down the west side, the city fanning east and south toward the Mexico border), with orange/red hot-spot blobs, densest in the SOUTH. RIGHT MONITOR: a simple bar chart and one rising line graph. Leave headroom above the kids' heads for the title.

# Layout

> Format as a 4×6 inch postcard in [portrait/landscape] orientation. Hero image fills
> 75% of the card with a bold headline [text] in [style-appropriate treatment] along
> the [top/bottom]. Small League logo in [corner]. Clean composition with generous
> margins. Print-ready quality.

# Additional Direction

STYLE: follow the FIRST reference (photo) for the composition and the SECOND reference ("AT HIS COMMAND") for the ART STYLE — bold, sharp, high-contrast FLAT comic art with completely smooth solid-color fills and clean black outlines. The whole image must be FLAT with NO texture, grain, or newsprint anywhere (including the border and background), exactly like the At His Command reference.

TEXT (render ONLY this, spelled EXACTLY, crisp):
- TITLE over the kids' heads: "ENGINEERS" in huge bold RED 3D block comic letters, heavy black outline, on a jagged BLUE starburst masthead — the AT-HIS-COMMAND lettering style.
- Cream caption box (black border, italic) just below the masthead: "Can Come From Anywhere ..."
- Cream square caption box (black border) over the BOY'S BACK, left: "... Help us find them"
- League logo over the GIRL'S BACK, right, ABOVE the bottom banner, sitting directly on the artwork with NO black or dark box behind it: "THE LEAGUE OF AMAZING PROGRAMMERS" stacked wordmark, orange "AMAZING", small lightning bolts, bar-lines over "OF".
- Bottom BANNER: a single cream strip running the FULL WIDTH across the very bottom edge, edge to edge, in SENTENCE CASE exactly: "Every student in San Diego should have a shot at a tech career."

Deep navy comic border frame (solid flat navy — no texture). NO robots. Exactly two mid-teen figures.

iterations.prompt:
A clean, modern, FLAT comic illustration — the same flat-poster look as the attached reference: bold sharp black linework, perfectly smooth flat color fills, simple hard-edged cel shading (at most two flat tones per surface), absolutely no texture/grain/gradient. This is the BACK of a postcard: a clean branded template, NOT a scene — no people, no computers, no illustration of any action.

The attached reference is the front of this same postcard — match its exact color language (deep navy/blue, warm cream, signal red/orange) and its lettering style, especially the small corner badge reading "THE LEAGUE OF AMAZING PROGRAMMERS" (cream rounded panel, tiny "THE LEAGUE OF", bold orange "AMAZING", cream "PROGRAMMERS" below).

LAYOUT — two horizontal zones filling a 4×6 inch landscape card (3:2 frame), stacked top to bottom:

1. TOP MASTHEAD BAND (about the top 20% of the card): a flat deep navy/blue field (matching the front's border blue) spanning the full width, carrying that SAME badge lettering scaled up into a full-width masthead: "THE LEAGUE OF" small, cream, centered; "AMAZING" huge and bold, orange, condensed caps, the dominant line; "PROGRAMMERS" medium, cream, below — all with confident black keylines, flat color, no gradients. A thin flat black rule separates this band from the zone below.

2. OPEN ZONE (the remaining ~80% of the card): ONE single, completely FLAT, EMPTY cream field spanning the full width down to the bottom edge — no texture, no gradient, no illustration, no decorative elements, and ABSOLUTELY NO TEXT of any kind. This area is intentionally left blank; message text will be added separately afterward.

A thin flat deep-navy or black rule border may run along the outer edge of the card, echoing the front's border treatment.

TEXT — the ONLY lettering anywhere on this card is the masthead "THE LEAGUE OF AMAZING PROGRAMMERS", spelled exactly as given. No other words, no placeholder text, no addresses, no stamps box, no postal markings, nothing else anywhere on the card.

FORMAT — 4×6 inch landscape postcard back, full-bleed, print-ready quality.
iterations.negative_prompt: Any people, computers, monitors, desks, or illustrated scene of any kind. Any text, lettering, numbers, or symbols in the cream zone below the masthead — it must be completely empty and flat. Placeholder text, lorem ipsum, sample address lines, a postage stamp box, postal cancellation marks, a QR code, barcodes. Texture, grain, gradient, noise, speckle, halftone, Ben-Day dots, newsprint, parchment, aged paper. Painted/airbrushed shading, soft glows, glossy highlights, 3D render, CGI, photorealism. A single-line masthead instead of the three-line stacked wordmark. Misspelled or reworded masthead text. Colors that don't match the front reference (no unrelated new hues). Anime or manga style, chibi proportions. Portrait orientation. Any element from the front-of-card scene (the two students, monitors, "ENGINEERS" burst headline, captions) appearing on this back template.
